In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the analysis of antibodies and with the characterization of the anti‐hapten antibody repertoire of a single cell clone.
the separation of anti‐dnp antibodies by two‐ dimensional affinity electrophoreses and the analysis of the separated antibodies.
the development of high resolution two‐ dimensional affinity electrophoreses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method is useful for separation of monoclonal antibody populations, and for the study of the heterogeneity of the affinity and pI of anti‐hap­ten antibodies in the population of the same specificity.
the two‐dimensional electrophoretic method developed in this study is a very powerful tool to separate antibodies into a large number of homogeneous IgG spots and to characterize them.
the present method is a powerful tool for the study of anti‐hapen antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single cell produces a number of antibodies of different pI, but of a similar or identical affinity to a specific antigen.

the high resolution two‐directional affinity electrophoretic method has made it possible to separate completely the anti‐hapten IgG antibodies from the same cell line, which are of different affinities to the hapten, and of a different pIs.
the two‐dimensional separation method is a very powerful tool for studying the heterogeneity of antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this method can separate anti‐hapten IgG molecules into families of the same affinity but different pI values.

the use of capillary isoelectrofocusing as first dimension in two‐dimensional electrophoresis allows the separation of proteins of a very high molecular mass, such as IgG, with a resolution which is superior to the one obtained by conventional two‐dimensional slab gel electrophoresis.
this method can be applied to the separation of other kinds of antibodies.
